questions.title: An unexpected sign-in link
questions.prompt: An unexpected email asks you to sign in urgently using its link. What is the safest next step?

answers.text: Open the service using a known bookmark or its official app.
answers.feedback: Use a route you already trust instead of the link in the unexpected message.

answers.text: Use the link because the message includes the company's logo.
answers.feedback: Logos can be copied. Branding alone does not establish that a message is genuine.

questions.title: Warning signs
questions.prompt: Which features of an unexpected email are reasons to verify it independently? Select all that apply.

answers.text: It asks for your password by email.
answers.feedback: Do not send passwords by email. Check the request through your organization's established channel.

answers.text: It pressures you to act immediately to avoid losing access.
answers.feedback: Pressure and urgency can be used to stop you checking a request carefully.
Correct spelling does not prove a message is genuine or fraudulent.
